calls.head: The Senators don’t own Woll
calls.body: Woll has been shaky against the Senators since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.

surprises.head: Samuel Ersson got lit up
surprises.body: Ersson allowed 6 goals on 19 shots, worth 2.0 expected goals: 4.0 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 150 starts. Most starters don’t get one a season.

story.head: York sparks the Flyers back from three down
paras: Never count the Flyers out. Cam York, who scores in about 1 game in 14, scored twice. Claude Giroux got the scoring started for the Senators less than two minutes in, but Owen Tippett made it 1-1 for Philadelphia on the power play just over two minutes later. The Flyers went more than 17 minutes without a shot on goal, from late in the first to late in the second, even with a power play in that stretch. Dylan Cozens put the Sens back ahead 2-1 early in the second, and Drake Batherson made it 3-1 on the power play midway through the period. York cut Ottawa’s lead to 3-2 late in the period. The third period brought five goals. Philip Tomasino and Cozens scored less than five minutes apart early in the period to push the lead to 5-2. York scored later in the period, and Tyson Foerster followed just 15 seconds after that to make it 5-4. With the goalie pulled and two and a half minutes left, Jamie Drysdale tied it 5-5. Travis Konecny won it 39 seconds into overtime. He finished with four points on a goal and three assists, and Drysdale had a goal and two assists.

The Senators had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Senators win about six in ten. Joseph Woll made 21 saves for the Flyers, and Samuel Ersson allowed six goals on 19 shots.
Porter Martone took three penalties on his own. The Flyers improved to 8-11-6 and climbed to fifth in the Metropolitan, while the Senators dropped to 14-6-3, slipping to third in the Atlantic.
